cases.statement: One hemizygous male (PMID 39484323), 14 years old, with cardiac-only disease leading to transplantation at 15.8 years.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: chest pain and exertional palpitations at 14; short PR interval and complete LBBB; biventricular hypertrophy (29.5 mm) with LGE fibrosis rising from 31.7% to 50%; LV apical thrombus and syncope with LVEF falling to 36%; heart transplantation at 15.8 years with glycogen-laden vacuolated cardiomyocytes

quotes.quote: A 14-year-old boy presented at the pediatric cardiology department due to oppressive chest pain, palpitations triggered by physical exertion, and daily headaches.
ECG showed sinus rhythm, short PR interval (102 milliseconds), and complete left bundle branch block (Figure 1B).
CMR demonstrated an LVEF of 50% with global biventricular hypertrophy, myocardial edema, along with late gadolinium enhancement quantified as 31.7% LV fibrosis.
Shortly after, the patient presented an episode of syncope.
Given the disease progression, and following guideline-directed management, the patient underwent heart transplantation at 15.8 years of age.
Histopathologic findings demonstrated cardiomyocytes with glycogen inclusions and cytoplasmatic vacuoles (Figure 4).
A hemizygous likely pathogenic variant was reported: LAMP2:c.645_651del (p.Lys215Asnfs25), resulting in diagnosis of Danon disease (DD).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Exclusively cardiac phenotype. A 289-gene clinical exome reported only this variant (no other findings are mentioned); Pompe disease was excluded by enzyme assay; no family history.

quotes.quote: A clinical exome with 289 genes related to this condition was requested.
A normal enzymatic activity assay of acid alpha-glucosidase excluded Pompe disease.
The patient had chronic daily headaches since 6 years of age, with no other significant personal or family history.
This paper presents the case of a 14-year-old boy with Danon disease exhibiting exclusive cardiac involvement, initially suspected as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

segregation.statement: Not reported; the paper states no family history and no relative testing.

quotes.quote: The patient had chronic daily headaches since 6 years of age, with no other significant personal or family history.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: 7-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Lys215AsnfsTer25)). The paper states loss of function is a known disease mechanism for LAMP2.

quotes.quote: The clinical exome sequencing confirmed a hemizygous deletion within the coding region of LAMP2, characterized by deletion of 7 nt between positions 645 to 651, causing frameshift and producing a truncated protein.

Genetic alterations in LAMP2, localized in Xq24, are the cause of this condition, following an X-linked inheritance pattern.^2 The gene codes for the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2, a glycoprotein in the lysosomal membrane, that when deficient, results in impaired macroautophagy.

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors say the variant has an extremely low frequency in gnomAD (no number given).

quotes.quote: and moderate pathogenic criteria due to its extremely low frequency in gnomAD population databases.

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify it as likely pathogenic under ACMG, citing a very strong null-variant criterion and a moderate rarity criterion (codes not named).

quotes.quote: This variant was classified as likely pathogenic according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics by fulfilling very strong pathogenic criteria, given that it is a null variant in a gene where loss of function is a known mechanism of disease, and moderate pathogenic criteria due to its extremely low frequency in gnomAD population databases.

concerns: Protein written inconsistently: the abstract gives 'p.LysAsnfs∗25' (no codon number) and the text 'p.Lys215Asnfs25' (no Ter); both match the predicted p.(Lys215AsnfsTer25) in substance.
No parental testing reported, so inheritance is unknown.
notes_for_panel: Single hemizygous male with a severe cardiac-only course and transplant histology consistent with Danon disease; no family studies.
